heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Global space economy estimated at ~$626B in 2026; Goldman Sachs and McKinsey both project a climb to $1.8T by 2035 alongside a rising wave of sector M&A

kpis.sub: BELOW POST-IPO HIGH · STARSHIP FLIGHT 14 SLIPS TO SEPT
kpis.label: SPCX recovered to ~$141.50 by Aug 30 — back above its $135 IPO price — but remains ~37% below its $225.64 post-IPO high; Starship Flight 14, the next major catalyst (first orbital flight, first tower-catch attempt, first Starlink V3 delivery), slipped from a targeted Aug 28 date to NET Sept 15-30 as Ship 41 and Booster 21 continue static-fire testing

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD STARTUP FUNDING · ALL-TIME RECORD, 4 MONTHS LEFT
kpis.label: Crunchbase-tracked global private investment in space/satellite startups hit a record $20.3B for 2026 as of Aug 29 — already the highest annual total on record with four months still to go; broader infrastructure-inclusive tracking (Space Capital) put H1 2026 alone at $67.7B, with Stoke Space still working to close its ~$1B Nova round and Rocket Lab drawing on its $3.6B Iridium bridge facility

kpis.sub: RKLB BACKLOG VS. STOCK NEAR A 12-MONTH LOW
kpis.label: Rocket Lab's record Q2 backlog reached $2.36B — bolstered by an Aug 4 $397M Space Force Flatellite (SB-AMTI) award on top of the NITE-STAR and Space Data Network wins — yet shares closed at $64.39 on Aug 28, ~57% below the $151 52-week high and testing the $67.50 floor of the Iridium exchange-ratio collar

tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

Shares recovered to ~$141.50 by Aug 30 — back above the $135 IPO price — still ~37% below the $225.64 post-IPO high

Neutron has logged 400+ Archimedes hot fires with a full engine set built for the first launch

rows.watch for: Deutsche Bank cut its price target to $268 from $285 on Aug 18, adding to leadership-transition overhang; shares near $262.82, about 44% below the $379.23 52-week high and just above the $258.54 52-week low; also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure

rows.watch for: No fresh company-specific catalyst this week to close that gap; insider-selling overhang; path to sustained profitability still the open question

rows.watch for: Shares near $11.27 (market cap ~$2.72B) against a 9-analyst average target of $14.56 (+34%); sustaining margin gains as revenue scales; no negative catalyst this week, holding up better than RKLB/LHX amid a choppy sector tape

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Root cause of the May 28 New Glenn pad explosion (a BE-4 main oxygen valve) remains under remediation at ULA's Decatur plant and Cape Canaveral, with NASA Stennis hot-fire testing set to begin this fall. Building out Pad 36A plus a second Cape Canaveral pad (36B), a new Vertical Integration Facility, and a government-partnered Payload Processing Facility for the larger New Glenn 9x4. Company remains "very committed" to a return to flight by year-end.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Record Q2 2026 revenue of $117.7M (+659% YoY, first quarter above $100M) on a record $1.5B backlog, alongside a $92.3M net loss; the quarter included a $144M NASA CLPS lunar-lander award, a $75M NASA JPL MoonFall subcontract, and a $94M Space Force radar-digitization contract. Shares remain well off their highs after Roth Capital's Aug 17 price-target cut to $45 from $60 on valuation concerns.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: Was targeting a close this month on its $1B round (Bloomberg, Aug 13) at a ~$9B valuation ex-new-money, on top of the $1.34B already raised, while expanding Moses Lake test facilities and activating Cape Canaveral's LC-14; no confirmation yet that the round has formally closed. First Nova liftoff still targeted for end of 2026.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rockets and constellations burn billions before returns — Stoke Space was still working to close its ~$1B raise as of late August on top of $1.34B already spent pre-launch; dilution and debt are chronic among small caps (RKLB's $3.6B Iridium bridge facility, ASTS's $1B convertible notes) — and ASTS's 15.5% single-day drop on Fed rate-hike chatter (Aug 28) shows how exposed debt-funded builders are to the rate cycle.

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: Much of the sector's revenue is NASA/DoD — the SDA's Golden Dome build-out (L3Harris/Sierra Space's $1.75B Tranche 3 award, RKLB's $397M Flatellite and $981M NITE-STAR ceiling) keeps flowing, but the Aug 17 CEO ouster at prime contractor L3Harris — followed by a Deutsche Bank price-target cut — is a reminder that governance and sentiment risk sit alongside budget risk in this concentrated customer base.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value / sector repricing
bear_case.description: A dominant incumbent with launch-cost leverage can compress everyone else's margins — SPCX has recovered above its $135 IPO price but remains ~37% below its post-IPO high, and its next real catalyst (Starship Flight 14) just slipped from Aug 28 to a mid/late-September window. Meanwhile record fundamentals across RKLB, RDW, LUNR and Firefly this earnings season haven't stopped RKLB from closing nearly 57% off its 52-week high — a widening gap between operating results and price that cuts both ways.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: One failed test or delayed launch can halve a small-cap, or push a manifest by months: Starship Flight 14 has already slipped from Aug 28 to a Sept 15-30 window as Ship 41 and Booster 21 complete static-fire testing, Rocket Lab's Neutron still hasn't flown, and Blue Origin's BE-4 root-cause finding shows how fast hardware failure can stall a program ahead of its promised year-end return to flight. SpaceX's own prospectus flags "key man" dependence on Elon Musk.

catalysts.title: SpaceX shares recover above the IPO price
catalysts.description: SPCX climbed back to ~$141.50, above the $135 IPO price, after trading as low as $137.90 during the week — still well off the $225.64 post-IPO high.

catalysts.title: Starship Flight 14 slips to September
catalysts.description: Super Heavy Booster 21 completed a full-duration 33-engine static fire, but the launch — targeted for Aug 28 — has slipped to a NET Sept 15-30 window as Ship 41 finishes its own engine-test campaign.

catalysts.title: AST SpaceMobile falls 15.5% on rate-hike risk
catalysts.description: Shares dropped after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signaled inflation is the Fed's focus, raising rate-hike odds; ASTS is building its constellation largely on borrowed money, making it unusually rate-sensitive.

catalysts.title: Rocket Lab closes near a 12-month low despite record backlog
catalysts.description: RKLB closed at $64.39 — down ~57% from its $151 52-week high — even after a record $2.36B Q2 backlog and the Aug 4 $397M Flatellite award, and is now testing the $67.50 floor of the Iridium exchange-ratio collar.

catalysts.title: SpaceX Starlink subscriber growth stays strong
catalysts.description: SpaceX continues adding 500,000-plus Starlink subscribers a month, with total subscribers at 12M — though ARPU is down 22% YoY as international and lower-priced plans scale.

catalysts.title: Deutsche Bank cuts L3Harris price target
catalysts.description: Target trimmed to $268 from $285, adding to sentiment pressure from the Aug 17 CEO ouster even as FY26 guidance holds and Sam Mehta settles into the CEO role.

etfs.name: Procure Space
etfs.summary: Pure-play, revenue-weighted (RKLB, PL, VSAT, MDA, ASTS top holdings); ~+31% YTD, +122% 1yr — RKLB's continued slide (~57% off its 52-week high) is now a larger drag on the fund given its weight, only partly offset by RDW's relative strength

etfs.name: ARK Space Exploration
etfs.summary: Actively managed, broader tech adjacency; roughly +11-28% YTD depending on pricing date, +67-76% 1yr — lagging the pure-play index funds

etfs.name: SPDR Kensho Final Frontiers
etfs.summary: Equal-weight, space + defense + deep-sea blend; ~+29-58% YTD, +100-131% 1yr depending on pricing date

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Record $2.36B backlog and the Aug 4 $397M Space Force Flatellite award confirm the government-revenue base, but shares closed at $64.39 on Aug 28 — down ~57% from the $151 52-week high — and are now testing the $67.50 floor of the Iridium exchange-ratio collar; trimming again since the price hasn't stabilized and Neutron's maiden flight remains unflown.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: FY26 guidance still holds and Sam Mehta's transition is proceeding without new operational red flags, but Deutsche Bank's Aug 18 price-target cut to $268 keeps sentiment soft on top of the Aug 17 CEO ouster; holding weight flat rather than adding until the transition shows more visible stability. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — don't double-count the exposure.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: Record Q2 revenue, record margin and record backlog carried no negative catalyst this week, and the stock has held up noticeably better than RKLB or LHX through a choppy sector tape; nudging weight up to reflect that relative resilience alongside the underlying execution.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: BlueBirds 11-13 launched successfully and backlog/MNO-partner metrics held, but the Aug 28 15.5% drop on Fed rate-hike chatter is a fresh reminder that ASTS funds its constellation largely on borrowed money; trimming to reflect that rate sensitivity on top of the existing convertible-note overhang.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Backlog and diversification (GEO satellite contract, EAGLE-VSWIR, Tranche 3 missile-defense build, Goonhilly/COMSAT) remain intact with no new catalyst this week either way; holding weight steady rather than chasing last week's move.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Shares recovered to ~$141.50 by Aug 30, back above the $135 IPO price, but the next real catalyst — Starship Flight 14 — just slipped from a targeted Aug 28 date to NET Sept 15-30, and the stock remains ~37% below its post-IPO high with more unlock tranches ahead through Dec 8, 2026. UK investors wanting SpaceX exposure without chasing the US listing can get indirect access via Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: The gap between the ~$19.98 share price and the analyst consensus target (now ~$40.10) has widened further, but that's sell-side sentiment, not a company-specific catalyst; no fresh contract or margin news this week to confirm the thesis, so still watch rather than own.

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Deal mechanics, not fundamentals, still drive this name: RKLB's S-4 isn't yet effective and RKLB shares are now trading below the $67.50 floor of the exchange-ratio collar, adding more uncertainty to what Iridium holders ultimately receive. RKLB stock remains the cleaner way to express the same view.
